climate.overview_html: The Copernicus C3S October 2026 bulletin officially confirms October was the warmest on record at 1.75°C above preindustrial, with global SSTs outside polar regions at 20.95°C — an all-time October high; 2026 is now “virtually certain” to exceed 1.5°C and “most likely” to rank second-warmest on record behind 2024. COP31 opens in Antalya in two days (November 9) against a backdrop of modest expectations: the US is attending through a congressional delegation only, not the formal negotiations, and a senior EU official warned a revolution is not to be expected. Australia and Türkiye have framed it as the first “Blue COP” with an Antalya Ocean Declaration planned for Energy Day, November 10.

items.headline: Copernicus Official: October 2026 Warmest on Record at 1.75°C Above Preindustrial; Global SSTs Highest for Any October; 2026 “Virtually Certain” to Exceed 1.5°C
items.summary: The official Copernicus C3S October 2026 monthly bulletin confirms October was the warmest on record globally at 1.75°C above preindustrial levels, with an average global surface air temperature of 15.35°C (0.90°C above the 1991–2020 mean). Sea surface temperatures outside polar regions reached 20.95°C — highest on record for any October, surpassing 2023. European land averaged 11.51°C, 1.49°C above normal, making it the second-warmest October on record for Europe. Copernicus declares 2026 'virtually certain' to exceed the 1.5°C Paris threshold, with a 20% chance of tying or exceeding 2024 as the hottest year on record. El Niño strengthening in the tropical Pacific is cited as the primary driver atop long-term warming.

items.headline: ‘Blue COP31’ Set to Spotlight Ocean Protections: Türkiye Plans Antalya Ocean Declaration; Australia Seeks Cover Decision on Oceans Within Formal Talks
items.summary: With COP31 two days away, Türkiye and Australia have framed the summit as the first 'Blue COP' — the host country is planning an Antalya Ocean Declaration, and Australia is seeking a formal cover decision on ocean protection within the UNFCCC process. Energy Day on November 10 is expected to feature ocean resilience commitments alongside electrification pledges. Pacific Small Island Developing States, whose Taku Pakasoa Declaration called for strengthened ocean protections, are positioned as the leading voices for ocean language. Climate finance and the fossil fuel transition remain the dominant negotiating battle lines.

items.headline: COP31 Faces Tough Test as Climate Threats Mount: US Sends Congressional Delegation Only; EU Warns Revolution Not Expected; Brazil’s Lula to Attend World Leaders’ Summit
items.summary: With COP31 days away, analysts and diplomats are framing the Antalya summit as a critical but difficult test. The US is attending through a congressional delegation and not the formal UNFCCC negotiations, a significant constraint on ambition given US emissions and financial commitments. A senior EU official warned that a revolution in climate action is not to be expected from Antalya. Brazil's president Lula is expected at the World Leaders' Summit on November 11–12, positioning Brazil — which presented a voluntary fossil fuel phase-out roadmap — as a potential bridge builder. Climate finance for the Global South, the NCQG successor mechanism, and fossil fuel transition language remain the core contested issues.

items.headline: COP31 Pre-Sessional Negotiations Open in Antalya; Main Session Opens November 9; Finance, Fossil Fuels and Adaptation Remain Core Battle Lines
items.summary: Technical pre-sessional negotiations for COP31 opened in Antalya on November 5 under Australian presidency (Australia's Chris Bowen leads the negotiations; Türkiye hosts). The three core battle lines entering talks: an NCQG on climate finance as a credible successor to the failed $100 billion-per-year pledge; language on fossil fuel phase-out following the UAE COP28 breakthrough; and whether adaptation finance receives a dedicated agenda item. The World Leaders Climate Action Summit is expected November 10–12. An oil refiner — Koç Holding's subsidiary Tüpraş — is the summit's top Global Business Partner, drawing criticism from climate campaigners.

items.headline: NOAA CPC El Niño Advisory: 70% Probability of Historically Large Event (RONI ≥ +2.5°C) for November–January 2026–27; Strong-to-Very Strong Through January–March 2027
items.summary: NOAA CPC's most recent ENSO Diagnostic Discussion puts the probability of a historically large El Niño event — defined as RONI of +2.5°C or more for the three-month average — at 70% for November–January 2026–27. This is the highest such probability stated in the current cycle and aligns with WMO's October projection of Niño 3.4 anomalies near +3.7–3.8°C for the same period. Strong-to-very strong El Niño conditions are assessed as likely through January–March 2027 with odds exceeding 83%. The next CPC ENSO Diagnostic Discussion is scheduled for November 12, 2026.

items.headline: Brazil Presents Voluntary Global Fossil Fuel Phase-Out Roadmap Ahead of COP31; Officials Stress It Is Not a Negotiating Text
items.summary: Brazil's government published a voluntary roadmap for a managed global fossil fuel phase-out ahead of COP31, framing it as a bridge proposal rather than a formal negotiating text. Brazilian officials stressed the plan accommodates different national energy security circumstances. The move positions Brazil — simultaneously a major oil exporter and one of the world's largest clean energy producers — as a potential dealmaker between major fossil fuel producers and climate-vulnerable nations at Antalya. The roadmap calls for a managed exit rather than an abrupt phase-out, echoing language from the UAE COP28 'transition away' compromise.

items.headline: Pacific Pre-COP Concludes with Taku Pakasoa Declaration: Faster Emissions Cuts, Accessible Climate Finance, Ocean Protection
items.summary: The Pacific Pre-COP concluded with the Taku Pakasoa Declaration. Pacific leaders — among the most climate-vulnerable nations — called for accelerated emissions reductions consistent with 1.5°C, more accessible direct climate finance for small island developing states, and strengthened protection of oceans as a global climate regulator. The declaration aligned with the COP31 Presidency's agenda of launching electrification pledges and adding ocean protection to the summit programme on Energy Day, November 10.

major_events.name: Florida Extreme Flooding — St. Johns River Spreading to Lake Harney, DeLand and Volusia County; Death Toll at Two; Major Flood Stage Forecast at Multiple Gauges
major_events.status: Escalating — Lake Harney forecast to approach major flood stage late next week as river continues rising through Seminole County; river reached moderate flood stage at DeLand in Volusia County and is continuing to rise; Cocoa gauge remains above 16.8 ft (threshold 16 ft); Sanford crest forecast 6.4 ft by Monday; two deaths confirmed statewide; Governor’s emergency declaration covers 14 counties
major_events.impact: Following the November 2 extreme rainfall event (up to 15 inches in Brevard County), the flood has spread northward through Seminole, Volusia and Lake counties and is now entering DeLand. Flood warnings now span the full river system from headwaters to its mouth near Jacksonville. Active cold front passage this weekend brings temporary rainfall relief but no reversal of the slow-drain river system; conditions expected to remain at or above flood stage through mid-November.

major_events.name: Tropical Storm Pena — Central Pacific, Southeast of Hawaiian Islands; No Land Threat
major_events.status: Active — Tropical Storm Pena formed on November 6 with 45 mph sustained winds, centered approximately 650 miles southeast of South Point, Hawai‘i; NHC Pacific forecasts westward track passing well south of the islands; no coastal watches or warnings in effect; model disagreement grows beyond Day 3
major_events.impact: Pena is developing within anomalously warm SSTs tied to the record 2026 El Niño event. While no land threat is currently forecast, the storm is in the same high-shear transition zone where El Niño systems have shown unexpected track variability this season. NHC Pacific is issuing advisory updates; next advisory expected to refine track uncertainty.

major_events.name: Southeast Asian Peatland Haze (Indonesia / Borneo / Sumatra) — Ongoing; Surface Hotspots Falling but Underground Fires Continue; Air-Pollution Deaths Up 42%
major_events.status: Easing at surface, persisting underground — Indonesia’s forest-fire hotspot count fell 67% in October as early wet-season rains began in parts of Sumatra and Kalimantan; however underground peat fires at depths of up to 8 m continue; Indonesia’s health ministry reported a 42% rise in air-pollution-linked deaths from August to September; bilateral Indonesia–Singapore task force operational
major_events.impact: ~40 million people region-wide continue to experience elevated PM2.5 across Indonesia, Malaysia, Singapore and the Philippines. The El Niño peak expected in December threatens to delay the full wet-season transition in the most fire-prone peatland areas of southern Sumatra and Central Kalimantan. Underground fires can persist for months despite surface rain onset.

weather.overview_html: Tropical Storm Pena formed on November 6 southeast of Hawai‘i with 45 mph winds; NHC Pacific forecasts no land threat. Florida’s flooding has spread further north: the St. Johns River hit moderate flood stage at DeLand in Volusia County and Lake Harney is forecast to approach major flood stage late next week; two deaths confirmed, 14-county emergency declaration in effect. Indonesia’s surface hotspot count fell 67% in October, but Indonesia’s health data shows air-pollution deaths rose 42% from August to September and underground peat fires continue.

items.headline: St. Johns River Flooding Spreads Further: Moderate Flood Stage Reached at DeLand (Volusia County); Lake Harney Forecast Major Flood Stage Late Next Week; Cocoa Gauge 16.8 ft
items.summary: As of November 7, the St. Johns River has reached moderate flood stage at DeLand in Volusia County, adding to the growing list of gauges above flood stage. The river near Lake Harney (Seminole/Volusia line) is now forecast to approach major flood stage late next week as slow upstream drainage continues. The Cocoa gauge (Brevard) remains at 16.8 ft, above its 16 ft flood stage threshold, with a continued rise toward major flood stage expected this weekend. Sanford is forecast to crest at 6.4 ft by Monday. Active flood warnings span the full river system. Two deaths have been confirmed statewide, with the Governor's emergency declaration covering 14 counties. A cold front is forecast to pass Saturday, bringing some temporary rainfall reduction without reversing the slow-drain river-flood trajectory.

items.headline: Tropical Storm Pena Forms Southeast of Hawaiian Islands; 45 mph Winds; NHC Pacific: No Land Threat; Track Uncertainty Grows After Day 3
items.summary: Tropical Storm Pena formed on November 6 with maximum sustained winds of 45 mph, centered approximately 650 miles southeast of South Point, Hawaii. NHC Pacific forecasts a westward track over the coming days, passing well south of the Hawaiian Islands with no coastal watches or warnings in effect. The storm is developing within anomalously warm El Niño-enhanced SSTs in the central Pacific. Forecast confidence drops after about Monday as computer models begin to diverge on the track. No impact to land areas is currently forecast. NHC Pacific advisories continue.

items.headline: Indonesia Forest-Fire Hotspot Count Falls 67% in October as Wet Season Begins; Air-Pollution Deaths Up 42% Aug–Sep; Underground Peat Fires at 8 m Depth Continuing
items.summary: Indonesia's surface forest-fire hotspot count fell approximately 67% in October as early wet-season rains began arriving in parts of Sumatra and Kalimantan. However, Indonesia's health ministry data shows air-pollution-linked deaths rose 42% from August to September 2026, with more than 170,000 people requiring treatment for acute respiratory infections in those two months. The 2026 fire season has burned over 1.9 million hectares through end-September, with the annual hotspot count exceeding yearly totals from every year 2019–2025. Underground peat fires at depths of up to 8 m resist wet-season rain onset and continue. The bilateral Indonesia–Singapore task force is operational, and Singapore has initiated action under its Transboundary Haze Pollution Act against firms contributing to the fires.

items.headline: Southwest US Flooding Aftermath: One Death Confirmed in Flagstaff; Damage Spans Four States; Cleanup Expected to Take Weeks
items.summary: One death confirmed in Flagstaff, Arizona, following the November 1–2 Four Corners atmospheric river event. Infrastructure damage spans Arizona, Colorado, New Mexico and portions of Nevada. Road closures, bridge damage and utility disruptions across Flagstaff, Sedona, Tucson, Durango and Pagosa Springs. More than 10 all-time flood gauge records broken across three states; full damage assessment ongoing. Cleanup expected to take several weeks. Attribution research examining the role of El Niño-elevated SSTs in amplifying atmospheric moisture flux is underway.

renewables.overview_html: Australian renewable developer Neoen secured its largest-ever financing — A$1.8 billion (~US$1.265 bn) — for a 1.2 GW portfolio of wind, solar and storage assets across South Australia, New South Wales and Western Australia. France awarded 1,006 MW in its latest onshore wind tender at a weighted average price of €78.57/MWh across 63 projects. China’s NEA reports that over 157 GW of large-scale wind and solar have been built in desert and barren areas by end-September 2026 — exceeding the country’s 2030 desert-category target seven years early. Türkiye’s YEKA GES-2026 auction awarded 785 MW of solar capacity across 11 projects.

items.headline: Neoen Secures A$1.8 Billion (~US$1.265 bn) Debt Financing for 1.2 GW Australian Renewables Portfolio; Largest Single Financing in Company History
items.summary: Australian renewable developer Neoen secured A$1.8 billion in debt from 13 Australian and international lenders for a 1.2 GW portfolio spanning five projects: two wind farms, two battery energy storage projects, and one solar farm. The assets are spread across South Australia, New South Wales and Western Australia. The 440 MWp Culcairn solar plant in New South Wales is among the named assets. Neoen says it has now raised more than A$5 billion since 2024, covering 4.7 GW across 20 Australian projects. The deal is the company's largest single financing to date and signals continued institutional appetite for large-scale Australian clean energy infrastructure.

items.headline: France Awards 1,006 MW in Onshore Wind Tender Across 63 Projects; Weighted Average Price €78.57/MWh
items.summary: France's energy regulator awarded approximately 1,006 MW of onshore wind capacity across 63 projects in its latest competitive tender. The weighted average awarded electricity price was €78.57 per MWh. The result adds to France's growing pipeline of awarded onshore wind capacity as the country accelerates its renewable buildout under EU energy policy commitments. Separate Belgian developer Virya Energy also features in this GreentechLead renewables roundup.

items.headline: China NEA: Over 157 GW of Large-Scale Desert Solar and Wind Built by End-September 2026 — Exceeds 2030 Target Seven Years Early
items.summary: China's National Energy Administration reported that more than 157 GW of large-scale wind and solar projects have been constructed in desert, Gobi, and other barren areas by the end of September 2026 — exceeding the country's 2030 target for the desert solar/wind programme by seven years. The figure does not represent China's total solar and wind installed capacity, which is substantially higher; it refers specifically to the large-base desert-siting programme. The milestone underscores the pace of China's renewable buildout and the compression of its project delivery timelines.

items.headline: Türkiye YEKA GES-2026 Auction Awards 785 MW Solar Capacity Across 11 Projects
items.summary: Türkiye's Ministry of Energy and Natural Resources awarded 785 MW of solar electricity connection capacity across 11 projects under its YEKA GES-2026 renewable-energy auction programme. The results expand Türkiye's solar installed base as the country hosts COP31 in November — a source of controversy given its reliance on fossil fuels — and reflect the country's stated long-term renewable energy expansion targets.

items.headline: India Targets 530 GW Renewable Energy Capacity by 2030 as Solar Manufacturing Expands to 225 GW
items.summary: Indian government officials confirmed an expanded target of 530 GW of renewable energy capacity by 2030, alongside plans to grow domestic solar module manufacturing capacity to 225 GW. The revised 530 GW figure encompasses solar, wind and hybrid capacity additions beyond India's previously stated 500 GW non-fossil power goal. Solar module manufacturing is to reach 225 GW capacity — up from approximately 74 GW in March 2025 — to reduce import dependence and position India as a global renewable equipment exporter.

items.headline: Sunraycer Renewables Acquires 325 MW of Solar Projects in Illinois and Missouri from Apricus Energy
items.summary: Sunraycer Renewables, a Crayhill Capital portfolio company, acquired two utility-scale solar projects from Apricus Energy: the 175 MW Gem City solar project in Adams County, Illinois, and the 150 MW Mighty Mississippi solar project in New Madrid County, Missouri. Construction on both facilities is anticipated to commence in early 2028. The acquisitions expand Sunraycer's growing MISO-region solar portfolio alongside its existing Texas solar-plus-storage assets financed in May 2026.

items.headline: Array Technologies and Shoals Technologies Agree All-Stock Merger; Creates Integrated Solar Infrastructure Platform Spanning Trackers and Electrical BOS
items.summary: Array Technologies (solar tracker systems) and Shoals Technologies (electrical balance of systems, connectors and BOS products) announced an all-stock merger agreement, creating an integrated solar infrastructure platform. The combined company will offer bundled procurement and single-vendor service for large-scale solar projects, targeting improved cost efficiencies for utility-scale developers. The deal is subject to shareholder and regulatory approvals.

items.headline: Tata Power Renewable Commissions 300 MW SECI Solar Project in Koppal, Karnataka; Total Renewable Portfolio Reaches 12 GW
items.summary: Tata Power Renewable Energy commissioned its 300 MW SECI-awarded solar project at Koppal, Karnataka, bringing the company's total renewable energy portfolio to 12 GW — a 20x growth over the past decade. The Koppal project is one of the largest single-site solar installations commissioned in Karnataka and directly supports India's national renewable energy targets.

items.headline: Squadron Energy Receives State Planning Approval for 420 MW Moreton Hill Wind Farm in Victoria, Australia; Up to 62 Turbines
items.summary: Squadron Energy received state planning approval for its 420 MW Moreton Hill wind farm in Victoria, which will incorporate up to 62 wind turbines. The approval is a key development milestone for one of Australia's largest renewable developers, contributing to Australia's target of 82% renewable electricity by 2030.

items.headline: US Interior Dept Seeks Court Reconsideration of Permits for Four Major Offshore Wind Projects Including 704 MW Revolution Wind and 1.7 GW Maryland Offshore Wind
items.summary: The US Interior and Justice Departments have sought court reconsideration of construction and operations plan approvals for at least four East Coast offshore wind projects: the 704 MW Revolution Wind (partly operational), the 1.7 GW Maryland Offshore Wind project, Atlantic Shores (NJ) and New England Wind (MA). ~300 wind and solar projects also await Department of Defense review.

science.overview_html: The standout new publication is a Nature study from Guan, Mackey, Cohen and colleagues introducing probabilistic bias correction (PBC), a machine-learning post-processor applied atop any dynamical or AI forecast model that doubled ECMWF’s AIFS-SUBS subseasonal skill score and placed first in ECMWF’s 2025 real-time forecasting competition across all variables and lead times. SATFRONT demonstrates that geostationary satellite data alone can detect atmospheric fronts over Europe (CSI@150 km = 0.428), rising to 0.591 when ERA5 reanalysis is added—relevant for data-sparse regions where full NWP reanalysis is unavailable. Among carried papers, Vonich & Hakim’s diagnostic framework separating initial-condition from model error in AI forecast degradation remains the most practically significant preprint of the period.

items.headline: Nature: Probabilistic Bias Correction Doubles Subseasonal AI Forecast Skill; Placed First in ECMWF 2025 Real-Time Competition; Open-Source Release
items.meta: Guan, Mackey, Cohen et al. · Nature (14 Oct 2026)
items.summary: A Nature study from Hannah Guan (Microsoft Research), Kyle Mackey (MIT) and colleagues introduces probabilistic bias correction (PBC), a machine-learning post-processing layer that corrects historical forecast distributions from any dynamical or AI model using adaptive bias correction across variables and lead times. Applied to ECMWF's AIFS-SUBS subseasonal model, PBC doubled the mean RPSS across all variables and lead times. PBC placed first for all weather variables and lead times in ECMWF's 2025 real-time subseasonal forecasting competition. Improvement is concentrated primarily in the tropical belt; gains over Europe are modest. Microsoft Research released the method as open-source software. The arXiv preprint (arXiv:2604.16238) dates from April 2026; the paper is now peer-reviewed and published in Nature.

items.headline: SATFRONT: Detecting Atmospheric Fronts from Geostationary Satellite Data Using Machine Learning; CSI@150 km = 0.428 Satellite-Only, 0.591 with ERA5
items.meta: Dravilas, Lucic et al. (30 Oct 2026) · NeurIPS 2026
items.summary: SATFRONT presents a machine learning framework for detecting cold, warm, and occluded atmospheric fronts over Europe from geostationary satellite observations, with ERA5 reanalysis as an optional additional input. Using Meteosat satellite data alone, the model achieves a Critical Success Index (CSI) at 150 km tolerance of 0.428; adding ERA5 raises this to 0.591. The analysis identifies near-surface winds and atmospheric moisture as the variables least recoverable from satellite observations alone — pointing to the specific limitations of satellite-only analysis in dynamically complex frontal zones. Developed in collaboration with EUMETSAT, the approach is relevant to operational NWP centres in data-sparse regions and to future satellite-first analysis workflows.

items.headline: arXiv:2611.05592 — Separating Initial-Condition vs. Model Error in AI Weather Forecasts: Attribution Framework for Downstream Probabilistic Skill Degradation
items.meta: Vonich & Hakim (3 Nov 2026) · arXiv:2611.05592 · cs.LG × physics.ao-ph
items.summary: This preprint by P. Trent Vonich and Gregory J. Hakim presents a diagnostic framework that disentangles initial-condition (IC) error from intrinsic model error in AI weather forecast degradation — a critical problem as AI models increasingly outperform physics-based counterparts on average metrics while showing unpredictable failure modes at longer leads. Evaluated on GraphCast and Pangu-Weather, the framework attributes probabilistic skill degradation at lead times beyond 5 days to specific IC error sources vs. model uncertainty. Results inform AI model development priorities and are a critical step toward principled uncertainty quantification for operational AI weather systems.

items.headline: arXiv:2611.01614 — Sonny-ENS: Score-Based Probabilistic Weather Forecasting Ensemble Outperforming IFS-ENS on CRPS at Lead Times Up to 10 Days
items.summary: Sonny-ENS applies a score-based diffusion approach to global probabilistic weather forecasting, generating ensembles by drawing samples from a learned conditional score function. The preprint reports that Sonny-ENS outperforms IFS-ENS on CRPS skill scores for lead times from 3 to 10 days, while maintaining ensemble spread calibration superior to other diffusion-based weather models. Addresses a key limitation of earlier diffusion weather models that trade ensemble sharpness against spread calibration.

items.headline: GRL: Accelerating Arctic Warming Now Inhibiting Net Land Carbon Uptake in Northern High Latitudes — Boreal Carbon Sink Weakening Signal
items.meta: Madani et al. · Geophysical Research Letters doi:10.1029/2026GL122135
items.summary: A GRL study finds that progressive warming is inhibiting net land carbon uptake in northern high latitudes, with moisture deficits, heightened soil respiration and permafrost carbon release outpacing vegetation productivity gains. The findings signal measurable weakening of the Arctic and boreal carbon sink, reinforcing the need to represent permafrost carbon processes in IPCC-class Earth system models and AI climate emulators targeting decadal projections.

items.headline: China CMA Deploys Two Operational AI Weather Systems: Typhoon Cloud-Pattern Recognition and 4-Hour Severe Convective Prediction Using Fengyun Satellite Data
items.summary: China's Meteorological Administration unveiled two new operational AI weather systems: a typhoon cloud-pattern recognition model interpreting storm structure from Fengyun satellite imagery in real time, and a model predicting severe convective weather up to four hours in advance. Both are deployed operationally within the CMA's national forecast suite, expanding the global footprint of fully operational AI weather systems alongside ECMWF's AIFS.

items.headline: arXiv:2610.40641 — Agentic AI Framework Connects Extreme-Weather Probabilistic Forecasts to Agricultural and Adaptation Impact Estimates End-to-End
items.summary: An agentic AI framework couples a weather-event detection module with an agricultural impact model, enabling automated end-to-end assessment from probabilistic forecast output to expected crop, livestock or infrastructure effects in near-real-time — addressing the critical gap between high-impact weather warnings and sector-specific impact projections.

items.headline: GRL: ‘Permafrost Detachment Slides’ — Climate-Driven Bottom-Up Failure Mode — Expected to Become More Frequent; 150+ Documented in Mackenzie Valley
items.summary: A GRL study identifies 'permafrost detachment slides' as a distinct bottom-up failure mechanism: slides fail from the base upward due to decades of ~0.3°C/decade permafrost warming combined with historic wildfire disturbance. The Mackenzie Valley alone has more than 150 such slides. Events of this type will become more frequent with continued warming, with implications for Arctic communities and infrastructure.

items.headline: arXiv:2610.38775 — FitzRoy: Reinforcement-Guided Diffusion Model Jointly Optimises Forecast Skill and Physical Realism for Continental US Precipitation
items.summary: FitzRoy applies reinforcement-guided diffusion to precipitation forecasting over the continental US, jointly optimising predictive skill and physical realism via a reinforcement learning reward signal. Standard diffusion-based weather models trade off sharp but physically implausible fields against smooth oversmoothed outputs; FitzRoy's RL guidance drives the diffusion process toward physically consistent outputs while retaining skill. Evaluated against MRMS radar observations and standard probabilistic metrics.

items.title: TPG Closes TPG Rise Climate II at $10.4 Billion Including $2.5 Billion for Global South Initiative; Second-Largest Climate Private Equity Fund to Date
items.body_html: TPG closed its second climate private equity strategy — TPG Rise Climate II plus the Global South Initiative (GSI) — at a combined $10.4 billion, per a Kirkland & Ellis advisory announcement and coverage in ESG Today. The close exceeds $10 billion for the main fund alone. The GSI earmarks $2.5 billion for climate investments in the Global South, meeting the target announced with ALTÉRRA at COP28 in 2023. 31% of commitments came from investors new to TPG. Early deployment has been rapid: TPG reportedly invested nearly one-third of the fund within a month of close. The inaugural Rise Climate fund closed in 2022 at $7.3 billion.

items.title: AP Ventures Closes Fund III at $300 Million for Low-Carbon Molecules: Green Hydrogen, Carbon Capture, Circularity and Hard-to-Abate Sectors
items.body_html: AP Ventures closed its third fund at $300 million (€270 mn), targeting early-stage industrial decarbonisation technologies including green hydrogen production, storage and transport; carbon capture and utilisation; and advanced recycling. The fund reached final close on October 28, 2026 from sovereign wealth funds, corporates, pension funds and family offices, both returning and new LPs. AP Ventures was spun out of Anglo American in 2018 and has backed 13 portfolio companies since Fund III's initial close. Its previous fund launched in 2021 at $316 million.

items.title: NextEra–Dominion $67 Billion Merger: Virginia SCC Evidentiary Hearing Set for November 17; Clean Virginia Motion to Compel Pending; Decision Expected January 11, 2027
items.body_html: The Virginia State Corporation Commission’s evidentiary hearing on the proposed $67 billion all-stock NextEra–Dominion merger is scheduled for November 17, 2026 in Richmond. Public hearings in Fairfax and Newport News drew large and divided crowds. SCC Hearing Examiner Roussy has yet to rule on a Clean Virginia motion to compel additional document production. The SCC’s final decision is expected January 11, 2027. The combined company would be the largest US electric utility by generation capacity, with significant implications for East Coast clean energy procurement and offshore wind contracting. Companies closed May 2026; deal expected to close H2 2027.

items.title: Sunraycer Renewables Acquires 325 MW of US Solar Projects in Illinois and Missouri from Apricus Energy
items.body_html: Sunraycer Renewables, a Crayhill Capital portfolio company, acquired two utility-scale solar projects from Apricus Energy on November 5: the 175 MW Gem City solar project in Adams County, Illinois, and the 150 MW Mighty Mississippi solar project in New Madrid County, Missouri. Construction on both projects is anticipated to commence in early 2028. The acquisitions expand Sunraycer’s MISO-region solar footprint alongside its existing Texas solar-plus-storage assets, adding to approximately 479.5 MW of Texas solar projects financed in May 2026.

items.title: Array Technologies and Shoals Technologies Announce All-Stock Merger; Creates Integrated Solar Infrastructure Platform
items.body_html: Array Technologies and Shoals Technologies announced an all-stock merger agreement on November 4, combining Array’s solar tracker systems with Shoals’ electrical balance-of-system products and wire harness connectors to create an integrated solar infrastructure platform. The combined company is expected to offer bundled procurement and single-vendor service for large-scale utility solar projects, targeting cost efficiencies across the hardware value chain. The deal is subject to shareholder and regulatory approvals.

items.title: Hull Street Energy Acquires FirstLight USA’s ~1.4 GW Hydro and Pumped-Storage Portfolio from PSP Investments
items.body_html: Hull Street Energy completed its acquisition of FirstLight USA’s U.S. generation business from the Public Sector Pension Investment Board (PSP Investments), taking on a ~1,400 MW clean power portfolio that includes the 1,168 MW Northfield Mountain pumped-storage facility in Massachusetts, 14 hydroelectric stations across Connecticut, Massachusetts and Pennsylvania, and three operational solar and battery facilities. Following the close, Hull Street holds approximately 1,200 MW of pumped storage hydro and nearly 400 MW of conventional hydro across the Northeast and Michigan.

items.title: Two Point O Capital Raises $10 Million Led by Transition Venture Capital to Scale Climate Intelligence Platform
items.body_html: Two Point O Capital raised $10 million in a funding round led by Transition Venture Capital, with participation from climate-focused co-investors. Two Point O provides climate intelligence and data analytics services for financial institutions quantifying physical climate risk in investment portfolios. The raise will be used to scale its data infrastructure and expand coverage from individual asset-level risk scoring to portfolio-level climate-adjusted valuations.

items.title: CESC/Purvah Green Extends ReNew 1.4 GWp Acquisition Deadline to November 21 — ~$510 M Deal Still Pending
items.body_html: India’s CESC Limited and its renewable arm Purvah Green Power have amended the share purchase agreement for their ~1.4 GWp ReNew Solar Power acquisition, extending the closing deadline 21 days to November 21, 2026. The deal covers six SPVs holding approximately 1.4 GWp of contracted operating solar capacity at an enterprise value of ~₹4,859 crore (~US$510 million), with more than 90% contracted with SECI.

items.title: BW ESS Acquires 200 MW/800 MWh French Battery Storage Portfolio from Recurrent Energy (Canadian Solar) — Enters Seventh Global Market
items.body_html: BW Energy Storage Systems acquired two ready-to-build standalone BESS projects in France from Canadian Solar’s subsidiary Recurrent Energy, comprising a 100 MW/400 MWh project at Baixas (Eastern Pyrénées) and a second 100 MW/400 MWh project at Coquainvilliers (Calvados). The deal marks BW ESS’s entry into France, its seventh market globally, adding to existing positions in the UK, Italy, Germany, Spain, Australia and the US.
